newsitem.title: USA: Hurricane Marco weakens as it nears Jamaica.
newsitem.headline: Hurricane Marco weakens as it nears Jamaica.

text.p: Jamaica braced for a battering on Wednesday but Hurricane Marco appeared to be weakening as it neared the Caribbean island's coast.

The Jamaican government issued a hurricane warning and urged residents to prepare for rough weather as Marco headed toward the island with 75 mile-per-hour (120 kph) winds. A hurricane watch was issued for Haiti and eastern of Cuba.
But the National Hurricane Centre in Miami said satellite images and data from a reconnaissance plane showed Marco had moved very little in the last few hours and central pressure had risen.
"If this weakening trend continues Marco may be downgraded to a tropical storm later today and warnings and watches will be revised," the centre said in a 1.30 p.m. EST (1830 GMT) bulletin.

The Jamaica Office of Disaster Preparedness said the island had already been lashed by heavy rains since Oct. 23, causing $3 million in damages to roads and drainage systems. About 170 families were without shelter because of flooding.

Disaster committees were on full alert, urging people to stock up on batteries and canned food. But there had been no rain in Kingston by midday on Wednesday and there was no sense of panic, residents said.

In the Dominican Republic, thousands of people had fled their homes for temporary refuge because of heavy rains, authorities said. Four hydroelectric dams had filled up and rivers were flooded with the overspill.
Wide areas were flooded including farmlands, Civil Defence Director Eugenio Cabral said. The army and police had been put on a state of alert.
At one p.m. EST (1800 GMT), Marco's centre was 200 miles (320 km) south of Kingston, Jamaica, at latitude 15 north and longitude 77.1 west, the National Hurricane Centre said.

It was moving northeast at 9 mph (14 kph) and was expected to near the coast of Jamaica on Thursday. It was dumping torrential rain of up 10 inches (25 cm) in its path, which could cause mudslides and rockslides, forecasters said.

On Tuesday, Nicaraguan civil defence authorities blamed at least two deaths on Marco after flooding washed away homes in the Pacific coast and northern regions. They said one person had died in a traffic accident and another by drowning.

Marco was upgraded from a tropical storm on Wednesday but it was a minimal hurricane, capable of flooding coastal roads and causing minor wind damage. A tropical storm graduates to hurricane status when maximum winds exceed 74 mph (119 kph).
This year's Atlantic hurricane season officially ends on Nov. 30.
